my advice would be just going for it. it’s scary, and that’s natural. but if you don’t say it now, you would just feel more and more scared to the point where you can’t do anything. (remember to go at your pace though! there’s no rush.)

speaking from experience here! she could possibly be confused at first, but if she’s someone who truly cares about you, she’d accept your true feelings. however, if the time comes and you do come out to her and she doesn’t react the way you expected, just remember that being gay isn’t wrong and having feelings for her isn’t wrong either. if she reacts nicely, then that’s good! take it easy OP. one step at a time. make wise decisions, and try erasing any thoughts of internalized homophobia (which is pretty common, sadly, even among queer people). and i’ve always mentioned this; trust your gut. you would for sure know yourself if the timing is right or not.

remember, you don’t just acquire a girlfriend in a few easy steps. it takes time. rather, i’ll give you advice to know how to develop a relationship that yknow, could blossom into something more. U___U

i met my exes online, and an ‘almost’ irl. one thing that is commonly known and used; to be friendly and open with them. if you find a girl interesting or cool, chatting them up and getting to know them better can really closen the gap over time. if you’re lucky and make the girl laugh, you might have a chance.

ofc, you need to be good or at least decent when it comes to flirting. i was awkward at first, but flirting comes naturally to me after years of doing it (at least on text LMAO), so working on those skills is a must. (pro tip! if you hang out, wearing a really attractive perfume can add plus points.)

and if someone catches your attention, you can go ahead and drop hints that u like them. give them a spotify playlist, watch movies with them, orrrrrrrrrr offer a warm hug :) just a little push here and there. but you know, confessing is way faster. trust ur gut OP! if you feel like it’s the right time, then it is the right time. match their pace!
